nodes.name: NM Surface Cleaning
nodes.procedure: NM was ultrasonicated with HCl for 10 min to remove nickel oxide on the surface, then rinsed with acetone, ethanol, and ultrapure water, respectively, and finally dried in air.
nodes.source_text: Before preparation, NM was ultrasonicated with HCl for 10 min to remove nickel oxide on the surface, then rinsed with acetone, ethanol, and ultrapure water...

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Mn-Ni/CoP
nodes.procedure: NiCl₂·6H₂O (0.01 mol), CoCl₂·6H₂O (0.01 mol), NaH₂PO₂·H₂O (0.025 mol), NH₄Cl (0.03 mol), MnCl₂·4H₂O (0.001 mol) were dissolved into DI water (100 mL) and stirring for 20 min to form a mixture solution, and the pH value was adjusted to three by dropping about HCl (37 wt.% 0.1 mL). To modulate the ratio of Mn doping, a series of molars MnCl₂·4H₂O (0.0005, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.005 mol) with different molar ratios of Co/Mn (20:1, 10:1, 5:1, 2:1) were added... One piece of the cleaned NM (1×2 cm²) was used as a working electrode, a platinum sheet as a counter electrode, and the standard Hg/HgSO₄ as a reference electrode. Mn-Ni/CoP was prepared by depositing at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻² for 15 min in the above solution, immediately followed by carefully rinsing with DI water and drying in air.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Surface Reconstruction
nodes.procedure: Mn-Ni/CoP was used as the working electrode for 100 CV cycles between -1.0 and -0.8 V versus reference electrode Hg/HgO in 1 M KOH with a carbon rod as the counter electrode, to obtain the r-Mn-Ni/CoP. After surface electrochemical activation, r-Mn-Ni/CoP was rinsed with ethanol and DI water three times respectively, and dried at room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Then, Mn-Ni/CoP was used as the working electrode for 100 CV cycles between -1.0 and -0.8 V versus reference electrode Hg/HgO in 1 M KOH...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn-Ni/CoP shows layered and granular morphology with cracks and bulges, tightly deposited on NM substrate with thickness ≈5 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There are some cracks and bulges in the Mn-Ni/CoP layer... From the cross-sectional SEM image, Mn-Ni/CoP is tightly deposited on NM substrate with a thickness of ≈5 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn-Ni/CoP exhibits uniform distribution of Co, Ni, P, and Mn elements; HRTEM reveals dispersed amorphous regions and crystalline NiP (0.183 nm, (221) plane) and CoP (0.196 nm, (112) plane) regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mn-Ni/CoP exhibits layered and granular morphology with uniform distribution of Co, Ni, P, and Mn... NiP and CoP coexist in crystalline regions, deducing from the lattice spacings of 0.183 and 0.196 nm corresponding to the (221) plane of NiP and the (112) plane of CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: r-Mn-Ni/CoP shows abundant nanoflakes perpendicular to surface; nanoflakes identified as Co(OH)₂ with lattice spacing 0.23 nm corresponding to (002) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Abundant nanoflakes with some perpendicular to the Mn-Ni/CoP surface are present in r-Mn-Ni/CoP... the nanoflakes display lattice spacing of 0.23 nm corresponding to the (002) plane of Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mappings confirm uniform distribution of Co, Ni, Mn, P in Mn-Ni/CoP and presence of Co and O in r-Mn-Ni/CoP nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: uniform distribution of Co, Ni, P, and Mn (Figure 1c,d; Figure S5, Supporting Information)... The element mappings reveal the existence of Co and O elements in nanoflakes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn-Ni/CoP shows only broad amorphous peaks between 25°-37° with disappearance of sharp Ni peaks, indicating full coverage and amorphous-crystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the sharp diffraction peaks of Ni (JCPDS, No. 70-1849, Figure S12a, Supporting Information) on NM disappear with only broad amorphous peaks between 25° - 37°.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn-Ni/CoP survey confirms Ni, Co, Mn, P presence; Mn 2p at 642.3 eV (2p3/2), 653.8 eV (2p1/2); P 2p P-M at 129.4/130.4 eV, P-O at 133.0 eV; Ni 2p3/2 Ni-P shifts +0.18 eV to 852.9 eV after Mn doping; Co 2p3/2 Co-P at 778.5 eV shifts +0.21 eV (Ni/CoP vs CoP) and +0.18 eV (Mn doping); r-Mn-Ni/CoP shows absent Co-P peaks and M-O at ~529.3 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey spectra in Figure 2b manifest the existence of Ni, Co, Mn, and P elements in Mn-Ni/CoP... The Mn 2p spectrum... at 642.3 eV and 653.8 eV... P 2p spectra... peaks at 129.4 and 130.4 eV correspond to P 2p3/2 and P 2p1/2 of P-M bond... 133.0 eV... P-O species... Ni 2p3/2 at 852.9 eV shows an obvious shift of 0.18 eV... Co-P peak at 778.5 eV... two meaningful shifts... The Co-P peaks at 778.5 and 794.7 eV were absent... M-O peak ≈529.3 eV was observed after surface reconstruction.

nodes.characterization_summary: r-Mn-Ni/CoP shows peaks at 495, 583, and 620 cm⁻¹ revealing coexistence of Co(OH)₂, CoOOH, and CoO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the three Raman peaks at 495, 583, and 620 cm⁻¹ further reveal the coexistence of Co(OH)₂, CoOOH, and CoO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: r-Mn-Ni/CoP shows contact angle close to 0° at 40 ms, indicating exceptional hydrophilicity from nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mn-Ni/CoP shows a contact angle of 47° at an interval of 40 ms, whereas the value is close to 0° under the same time for r-Mn-Ni/CoP, manifesting the exceptional hydrophilicity originating from the rich nanoflakes.

nodes.evidence_snippet: the critical binding force of r-Mn-Ni/CoP (3.46 N) is significantly higher than that of Pt/C (1.81 N).
